Review PR https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokedex/pull/6245 for correctness bugs. The branch `claude/30-obvious-tasks-hyei7t` is checked out at /Users/harshanandiwada/workspace/pokedex-6245 (work only there; diff with `git diff origin/main...HEAD`). Read-only: do not edit, commit, push, or comment on GitHub.

What the PR does: ~29 WMS get_* functions stop hiding the next window's start inside their page token. Now the token carries only the in-window page/cursor, and a finished window returns `next_token=None, next_start=window_end` (the shape Finale `get_orders` uses). Watermark functions (dcl, extensiv-3pl-central, ffe, infoplus, shipstream, shiphero products) return a `next_start` once the watermark crosses a UTC day boundary. Read the crawler loop that consumes `next_token` / `next_start` / `crawl_start_overlap_minutes` before judging (grep for `next_start` outside integrations/).

Owner's policy, which is deliberate:
- Each function reads ONLY its new token shape, hard-indexed. A token saved before deploy in an old shape crashing the crawl is fine (reset by hand). Do not flag missing backward compatibility or suggest handling two token shapes.
- Re-crawling some data twice is fine.
- What matters: bugs in the new code, and quiet failures (infinite loops, a window that never advances, a next_start that doesn't move forward, data skipped without an error, next_start returned together with a next_token, the last window of the range never finishing, etc.).

Known class of bug to hunt for: the page token shape was changed late (e.g., bergen, packiyo orders/products, shiphero get_inbound_shipments, stord get_orders were flattened from single-key dicts like {"page": n} / {"after": cursor} to a plain int or cursor string). Bergen had `next_token = {"page_number": page_token + 1}` left behind after its default became `page_token=1` (now fixed in 537cf69). Check every converted function for mismatches between the default page_token, how it's read, and what next_token is set to on every branch, since live tests only exercise page 1. Also check window math (tz-aware vs naive, microseconds, window_end past end, windows shorter than crawl_start_overlap_minutes), and that every return path includes the right keys.

Run targeted tests only if useful (`yarn test -k <name> --<resource> --gets`, see .claude/skills/run-scripts; never raw pytest).

Report: a list of confirmed bugs, most severe first, each with file:line, the concrete input/state that triggers it, and the one-line fix. Then a short list of anything plausible but unconfirmed. Skip style nits.

<system-reminder>
Your final report is delivered through SubagentHandback: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}) and then stop. Only a SubagentHandback call reaches your caller as your result; plain text you write at the end is not delivered.
</system-reminder>

# Trackstar - Integration Platform

## Project Overview

Trackstar unifies e-commerce and logistics integrations into normalized APIs.

**Components:**

- **pokedex** (Python/Flask) - Core API backend (port 8000)
- **eevvee** (React) - Auth modal (port 3005)
- **pokecenter** (React) - Admin dashboard (port 3000)

## Quick Start

```bash

yarn serve        # flask API
yarn worker       # celery worker
yarn test         # run tests
yarn crawl        # test integration method
yarn generate     # scaffold new integration
```

## Project Structure

```txt
trackstar/
├── pokedex/          # backend (Flask, Celery)
│   ├── integrations/ # integration code (wms/, cart/, freight/)
│   ├── resources/    # marshmallow schemas
│   └── test/         # test suites
├── eevvee/           # auth modal (React)
├── pokecenter/       # admin UI (React)
└── .claude/
    ├── knowledge/    # integration examples index
    ├── skills/       # reusable workflows
    ├── commands/     # slash commands
    ├── schemas/      # resource field definitions
    └── plans/        # implementation plans (gitignored)
```

## Code Style

- no docstrings - code is self-documenting
- minimal comments (lowercase, 5-10 words, explain why not what)
- favor simplicity over cleverness
- error-driven development - let errors guide fixes, try not to use .get
- avoid list comprehensions and code like formatted_inventory.append(format(item)) - separate into multiple lines for readability and easier debugging (e.g formatted_item = format(item); formatted_inventory.append(formatted_item))
- for pokedex - if "created_date" and "updated_date" are not implemented, don't add it in the integration formatter code. don't add trackstar_tags either

## Integration Development

1. Read `.claude/knowledge/integration-examples.md` to find similar integrations
2. Study the actual implementation code (always up to date)
3. Use `/plan-integration` for complex work
4. Test incrementally with `yarn crawl`

**IntegrationNotImplemented vs None:**
- `IntegrationNotImplemented` means the field is not available at all from the integration — no endpoint or data source provides it
- If even one code path provides a field, all other paths must set it to `None`, not `IntegrationNotImplemented`
- There will never be a case where we see code like `x = y or IntegrationNotImplemented` or `x = data.get(y, IntegrationNotImplemented)`

## Testing

After making changes, run targeted tests. See `run-scripts` skill for filter options.

**Exemplar integrations:**
- WMS: deposco, shipbob, ongoing
- Cart: shopify, etsy, amazon

## Available Commands

- `/catchup` - review branch changes
- `/plan-integration` - start integration planning
- `/pr` - prepare pull request
- `/debug-report` - investigate customer issues
- `/generate-support-email` - draft email to WMS/API vendor

## Available Skills

- **scrape-docs** - scrape API documentation into LLM-optimized markdown
- **validate-api** - test API auth and collect samples before implementation
- **run-scripts** - reference for crawl, test, curl, serve, generate commands
- **review-code** - code review checklist for production readiness
- **issue-debugging** - investigating trackstar issues (missing data, webhooks, sync, stale schedules, errors)
- **worktree** - manage git worktrees for feature branches (`/worktree add|remove branch-name`)

## Context Management

- clear context at 60k tokens (use /clear)
- for complex tasks: document progress to .md, clear, continue
- read knowledge files on-demand, don't preload
- use Planning Mode for complex integration work

## Working Directories

- plans go in `pokedex/../.claude/plans/` (gitignored)
- temp scripts go in `pokedex/../.claude/tmp/` (gitignored)
- scraped docs go in `pokedex/../.claude/references/{integration}/` (gitignored)

# Trackstar - Integration Platform

Trackstar unifies e-commerce and logistics integrations into normalized APIs.

**Components** (each sibling repo has its own `CLAUDE.md` for its stack and deploys; read the one for the repo you're in):

- **pokedex** (Python/Flask): core API backend, port 8000. This file.
- **eevvee** (React): customer-facing auth modal, port 3005. [trackstarhq/eevvee](https://github.com/trackstarhq/eevvee)
- **pokecenter** (React): customer admin dashboard, port 3000. [trackstarhq/pokecenter](https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokecenter)
- **oak** (Next.js): internal observability and admin, port 3000, runs separately from pokecenter. [trackstarhq/oak](https://github.com/trackstarhq/oak)
- **documentation** (Mintlify): public docs at docs.trackstarhq.com. [trackstarhq/documentation](https://github.com/trackstarhq/documentation)

## Quick Start

```bash
yarn serve        # flask API
yarn worker       # celery worker
yarn test         # run tests
yarn crawl        # test integration method
yarn generate     # scaffold new integration
```

## Where to look

| Need | Path |
|---|---|
| Integration code | `integrations/{wms,cart,carrier}/{name}/` |
| Canonical schemas (the only source of truth, never copied elsewhere) | `resources/{type}/*.py` |
| Full rules for integration code | `.claude/references/integration-patterns.md` |
| Example integrations by API shape (auth, pagination, enrichment) | `.claude/knowledge/integration-examples.md` |
| Known integration quirks | `.claude/knowledge/integration-gotchas.md` |
| Per-integration API notes | `.claude/references/{name}/api-summary.md` |
| Yarn script flags (test, crawl, curl, install) | `.claude/skills/run-scripts/` |
| How a subsystem works, in any trackstarhq repo | `knowledge-base` skill (Greptile) |
| What Greptile reads on a PR | `.greptile/files.json` |
| Skills, subagents, slash commands | `.claude/skills/`, `.claude/agents/`, `.claude/commands/` |

## Code Style

Full rules: [`.claude/rules/code-style.md`](rules/code-style.md). The short version:

- No docstrings outside the exceptions listed there. No comment unless the code can't explain itself; a kept comment is lowercase, plain, and says why, not what.
- No leading-underscore names. Reuse the codebase's existing verbs and status words; grep before naming.
- Avoid `.get` defaults (let missing data fail loudly). No comprehensions in integration code. Follow the `logger`/`print` rules.
- Constants live in `config.py` (`import config`, not scattered `os.environ.get`).
- Canonical schemas (`resources/<type>/*.py`) never name vendors. Keep "NetSuite", "Shopify", etc. inside `integrations/`.

## Integration Development

**Freight integrations are out of scope.** Decline to build one; existing freight code is maintained but not extended.

1. Find a similar integration in [`.claude/knowledge/integration-examples.md`](knowledge/integration-examples.md). Pick by API shape (transport, auth, pagination), not by type.
2. Read that integration's actual code.
3. `/plan-integration` builds a new integration; `/iterate-integration` adds or fixes a function.
4. Test as you go with `yarn crawl`.

**Read [`.claude/references/integration-patterns.md`](references/integration-patterns.md) before any non-trivial integration edit.** It is the full pass/fail checklist the reviewer enforces. These rules load automatically when you touch integration files:

- [`.claude/rules/integration-fidelity.md`](rules/integration-fidelity.md): represent the source API faithfully. Fail loudly instead of working around quietly, find the root cause first, `IntegrationNotImplemented` vs `None`, date and `trackstar_tags` rules.
- [`.claude/rules/write-safety.md`](rules/write-safety.md): `allow_writes()` / `test_account()`. Never write to a vendor's production account; what matters is the effect on vendor data, not the HTTP method.
- [`.claude/rules/integration-testing.md`](rules/integration-testing.md): the live `TestX` class is the only test surface. Never change a failing test to make it pass.

## Testing

`yarn test` with filters is the only way to run tests. Never `python -m pytest` or raw `pytest`. For ad-hoc Python use `uv run python3`, never raw `python3`. Flags are in the `run-scripts` skill.

## Working

- Git rules: [`.claude/rules/git-workflow.md`](rules/git-workflow.md). PR rules: [`.claude/rules/pull-requests.md`](rules/pull-requests.md).
- For multi-phase work, keep progress in a plan and `/clear` between phases. Use plan mode for new integration work or unclear scope.
- Read knowledge and reference files when you need them, not up front.
- Plans go in `.claude/plans/`, temp scripts in `.claude/tmp/` (both gitignored).
- Scraped docs go in `.claude/references/{integration}/`. `api-summary.md` and text notes are committed; bulky or binary sources are not (`*.xsd`, `*.pdf`, `openapi*.json`, `*.postman_collection.json`, `samples/`, `sample_*.json`, `spec_extract/`). `git check-ignore -v <path>` settles a specific file.

# Git workflow

- **Never commit directly to `main`** — all work goes on feature branches.
- **Create the branch BEFORE any code changes** — a prerequisite, not a post-step. When planning, name the branch upfront in a "Setup" section.
- If the user specifies a **worktree**, `cd` there before any file operations.
- Branch naming: `{feature-or-fix-description}` (e.g., `extensiv-inbound-lot-number`).
- **Keep a PR branch rebased on `origin/main`** — reviewers expect linear history and will ask for a rebase before approving; no merge commits on a PR branch. Rebase only branches you own, never someone else's.

# Communications: customer, vendor, Linear, and PRs

Applies to anything another person reads: support emails (`/generate-support-email`), customer replies, Slack to CSMs, vendor support threads, Linear issues and comments, Pylon notes, and PR titles, descriptions and review replies.

## Brevity is the default

Short by default. If a sentence can go without losing a fact the reader needs to act, cut it. These are ceilings, not targets; go over only when the extra length carries something the reader must have:

- **PR description:** one lead line on what changed and why, one short paragraph of context, a tight list of changes, one line on how it was verified. No pitch, no file-by-file restatement of the diff. Drop any section that would be empty or obvious.
- **Linear issue or comment:** the finding and the action in one to three sentences. Bullets only for list data (ids, affected connections), never for prose. This binds cards a skill files too; see [Linear cards](#linear-cards).
- **Slack, customer or vendor reply:** the answer first, in two to four sentences. Add detail only if the reader needs it to act.
- **Review reply:** the decision and its one reason. Don't repeat their comment back.

When in doubt, send the shorter version. The reader can ask for more.

## Linear cards

A card asks a person to do something. It is not a place to store an investigation. Most readers see only the title and the first two lines, so those must carry the whole ask.

- **File a card only when a person has to act.** If a PR is what the reviewer needs, open the PR and skip the card. If the problem fixes itself, or a comment on an existing card covers it, do that instead.
- **Body: the finding and the action**, within the ceiling above. No section headers ("Root cause", "Evidence", "Next steps"); a card that needs them is too long.
- **Evidence goes in the first comment, not the body:** log lines, raw vendor responses, Datadog links, crawl output, counts, tracebacks, before/after tables.
- **A card is filed exactly as written.** Nothing rewrites a skill's card after it is composed, so the skill writes the final text.
- **Write for a developer who has never opened `.claude/`.** No internal codes or field names where a plain phrase works. Say "the crawl restarts from the beginning every time", not "page_token == current_crawl_end wedges the walk".
- **Title: `{integration or area}: <what is wrong>`.** Specific enough to tell two cards apart, sentence case, no trailing punctuation, no ticket id, no status prefix.
- **One card per decision a person must make.** Not one per run or per log line. Run summaries go in the Slack thread or the PR.
- **Machine-read blocks** (a fenced block that tooling reads back) are exempt from the ceiling, but keep their free-text fields to a sentence each.

## Sound like a person

- **No em-dashes** (`—`, `–`). Use a comma, period, parentheses, or colon.
- **Plain words, one-read test.** A smart reader who didn't write the code should get each sentence in one pass. Say what happens, not how the internals are wired. No chains of internal names (`api_write_resource → validate_body → schema.load`), no noun stacks ("the write-validation boundary"), no framework vocabulary. Write "the limit is checked when the request comes in, before any file is sent".
- **Lead with the point**, then the detail. Short paragraphs.
- **Be concrete:** real order ids, error messages, timestamps, endpoints, PR and issue numbers.
- **Cut AI tells:** no "I hope this finds you well", "Certainly!", reflexive "Let me know if you have any questions!", over-hedging, bullet lists for everything, or filler words ("delve", "leverage", "robust", "seamless", "in order to").
- **One acknowledgement, no over-apologizing.**
- **Links:** on markdown surfaces (PRs, Linear) write `[label](url)`, never inside backticks (that shows as literal text). Slack uses `<url|label>`. Plain email gets the bare URL.
- **Match the surface:**
  - Vendor support: technical and exact. What you called, what came back, what you expected.
  - Customer: plain language, no internal terms, clear next steps.
  - Linear: the finding and the action, no preamble.
  - PRs: the title says what changed and why; the body is context, changes, and verification. Never mention the authoring agent or that an LLM wrote it.

# Pull requests (pokedex)

## CI test scope

Every PR body sets the CI test scope with a line `.github/workflows/ci.yml` parses, in exactly this form:

    test override: `yarn test <args>`

`-s` is not a scope. It tells the `suggest-tests` CI step there is no override, so it picks the args from the diff: `-k <name>` for each changed integration when only integration files changed (and it rewrites the line in the PR body to match), otherwise the full run. Anything other than `-s` is used exactly as written, including a bare `yarn test`. Do **not** add a `<!-- auto-tests -->` marker: CI treats a marked line as its own and will overwrite it.

- **Integration PR** (touches `integrations/{type}/{name}/` and/or `test/integrations/{type}/{name}_test.py`): `test override: ` `yarn test -k <name>`. The integration name only, nothing before `-k`. A stale-schedule or single-integration fix is always one integration; a change that reaches the framework is a non-integration PR.
- **Multi-integration sweep** (a `/fix-tests` run touching several integrations and nothing else): one `-k` per changed integration, `test override: ` `yarn test -k <a> -k <b> -k <c>`. `scripts/test.py` maps each `-k` to its test file.
- **Non-integration PR** (anything else: `utils/`, `resources/`, `celery_tasks/`, `config.py`, `lambda_handlers/`, `api.py`, `scripts/`, …): `test override: ` `yarn test`. With no scope arg, `scripts/test.py` hands pytest no path, so the run covers the whole `test/` tree: the integration suite **and** `api` / `celery` / `lambda` / `utils` / `transports`. Shared code is exactly what can break an integration, so that is the scope you want. Narrow it only when the blast radius is provably smaller: `nonints` when the change cannot reach integration code at all, or `-k <name>` when it reaches exactly one integration (say a `config.py` constant only it reads). Say why in the PR body.
- **Letting CI pick** (`yarn test -s`, the template default): only when you want `suggest-tests` to choose. It picks the same thing the rules above would, so writing the override yourself is clearer.
- **No test-affecting change** (docs, markdown, config only): put `[skip-tests]` in the body.

**Why:** a bare `yarn test` is the widest run. It is slow and hits real or sandbox vendor APIs, and that cost is worth paying whenever a change can reach integration code. `-k <name>` trades coverage for speed on a diff confined to one integration; `nonints` does the same for a diff that cannot touch integrations. Narrowing is a claim about blast radius, so make it on purpose, not by habit.

## Ship on merge

The ship block in the PR template (between the `<!-- ship-on-merge -->` markers) is a deploy request. When a PR is merged with a stage and at least one service ticked, `ship.yml` runs for exactly those services and comments on the PR with the run, commit, request, and who merged. Ticking both stages starts two independent runs; a dev failure doesn't stop prod.

- **An untouched block ships nothing.** Agents never tick a box and can't approve or merge their own work. Leave the boxes for the person who merges.
- **Copy the block from `.github/pull_request_template.md` verbatim; never retype it.** The merge run checks ticked names against that file, so a hand-typed list breaks when a service is added.
- **Read the boxes before you merge.** Anyone with write access can tick one, and GitHub doesn't show the workflow who did. The person who merges owns the release. Prod ships are recorded, not gated.
- **Ticking `crawler` kills running crawls.** They restart only after their heartbeat goes stale (up to 10 minutes). Most resume from their saved page; a few integrations opt out and start over.
- **Service names are `config.SERVICES` keys.** A wrong name fails the merge run. `test/utils/ship_on_merge_test.py` keeps the boxes and config in sync.

## Investigation and fix PRs

- **The diff must contain the fix the body describes.** A fix PR with an empty or unrelated diff gets closed. Before opening, check the branch carries the change and that `main` doesn't already have the same fix.
- **Include the raw data behind the diagnosis** (source API rows, log lines, or the Datadog query, with customer PII removed), so a person can check it without redoing the investigation. A few lines can go in the body; anything longer goes in a PR comment so the body stays short.

## Draft vs open

Greptile reviews only non-draft PRs. Open ready for review when an automated pass helps the next human reader; open as a draft when it would be noise.

- **`plan-integration` builds: ready for review.** The body's "Review this first" list says what the automated pass can't judge. An aborted run (`[NOT READY]` title) opens as a draft.
- **Other integration PRs (`iterate-integration`, `wrap-integration`): draft**, until a person reads it and marks it ready.
- **Stale-schedule PRs (`stale-schedule-investigate`): ready for review.** They are small and root-caused.
- **Everything else: the author's call.** Draft while in progress, ready when it is.

The bot account applies this on its own (`.claude/bot-account.md`).

- [APM trace gluing investigation](project_apm_trace_gluing.md) — open: many Lambda invocations sharing one trace_id on warm PC containers, suspect ThreadPoolExecutor + ddtrace
- [Link-test compensating validation](feedback_link_test_compensating_validation.md) — resolve BOTH id sets of a failing link test symmetrically, not just one side
- [Frivolous PR annotations](feedback_frivolous_pr_annotations.md) — fix-tests/iterate PRs shouldn't add api-summary AMENDED sections or comments for simple fixes

## Code Style

Full rules: [`.claude/rules/code-style.md`](rules/code-style.md). The short version:

- No docstrings outside the exceptions listed there. No comment unless the code can't explain itself; a kept comment is lowercase, plain, and says why, not what.
- No leading-underscore names. Reuse the codebase's existing verbs and status words; grep before naming.
- Avoid `.get` defaults (let missing data fail loudly). No comprehensions in integration code. Follow the `logger`/`print` rules.
- Constants live in `config.py` (`import config`, not scattered `os.environ.get`).
- Canonical schemas (`resources/<type>/*.py`) never name vendors. Keep "NetSuite", "Shopify", etc. inside `integrations/`.

## Integration Development

**Freight integrations are out of scope.** Decline to build one; existing freight code is maintained but not extended.

1. Find a similar integration in [`.claude/knowledge/integration-examples.md`](knowledge/integration-examples.md). Pick by API shape (transport, auth, pagination), not by type.
2. Read that integration's actual code.
3. `/plan-integration` builds a new integration; `/iterate-integration` adds or fixes a function.

**Read [`.claude/references/integration-patterns.md`](references/integration-patterns.md) before any non-trivial integration edit.** It is the full pass/fail checklist the reviewer enforces. These rules load automatically when you touch integration files:

- [`.claude/rules/integration-testing.md`](rules/integration-testing.md): the live `TestX` class is the only test surface. Never change a failing test to make it pass.

`yarn test` with filters is the only way to run tests. Never `python -m pytest` or raw `pytest`. For ad-hoc Python use `uv run python3`, never raw `python3`. Flags are in the `run-scripts` skill.

# Git workflow

- **Never commit directly to `main`** — all work goes on feature branches.

# Communications: customer, vendor, Linear, and PRs

Applies to anything another person reads: support emails (`/generate-support-email`), customer replies, Slack to CSMs, vendor support threads, Linear issues and comments, Pylon notes, and PR titles, descriptions and review replies.

## Brevity is the default

Short by default. If a sentence can go without losing a fact the reader needs to act, cut it. These are ceilings, not targets; go over only when the extra length carries something the reader must have:

- **PR description:** one lead line on what changed and why, one short paragraph of context, a tight list of changes, one line on how it was verified. No pitch, no file-by-file restatement of the diff. Drop any section that would be empty or obvious.
- **Linear issue or comment:** the finding and the action in one to three sentences. Bullets only for list data (ids, affected connections), never for prose. This binds cards a skill files too; see [Linear cards](#linear-cards).
- **Slack, customer or vendor reply:** the answer first, in two to four sentences. Add detail only if the reader needs it to act.
- **Review reply:** the decision and its one reason. Don't repeat their comment back.

When in doubt, send the shorter version. The reader can ask for more.

## Linear cards

A card asks a person to do something. It is not a place to store an investigation. Most readers see only the title and the first two lines, so those must carry the whole ask.

- **File a card only when a person has to act.** If a PR is what the reviewer needs, open the PR and skip the card. If the problem fixes itself, or a comment on an existing card covers it, do that instead.
- **Body: the finding and the action**, within the ceiling above. No section headers ("Root cause", "Evidence", "Next steps"); a card that needs them is too long.
- **Evidence goes in the first comment, not the body:** log lines, raw vendor responses, Datadog links, crawl output, counts, tracebacks, before/after tables.
- **A card is filed exactly as written.** Nothing rewrites a skill's card after it is composed, so the skill writes the final text.
- **Write for a developer who has never opened `.claude/`.** No internal codes or field names where a plain phrase works. Say "the crawl restarts from the beginning every time", not "page_token == current_crawl_end wedges the walk".
- **Title: `{integration or area}: <what is wrong>`.** Specific enough to tell two cards apart, sentence case, no trailing punctuation, no ticket id, no status prefix.
- **One card per decision a person must make.** Not one per run or per log line. Run summaries go in the Slack thread or the PR.
- **Machine-read blocks** (a fenced block that tooling reads back) are exempt from the ceiling, but keep their free-text fields to a sentence each.

## Sound like a person

- **No em-dashes** (`—`, `–`). Use a comma, period, parentheses, or colon.
- **Plain words, one-read test.** A smart reader who didn't write the code should get each sentence in one pass. Say what happens, not how the internals are wired. No chains of internal names (`api_write_resource → validate_body → schema.load`), no noun stacks ("the write-validation boundary"), no framework vocabulary. Write "the limit is checked when the request comes in, before any file is sent".
- **Lead with the point**, then the detail. Short paragraphs.
- **Be concrete:** real order ids, error messages, timestamps, endpoints, PR and issue numbers.
- **Cut AI tells:** no "I hope this finds you well", "Certainly!", reflexive "Let me know if you have any questions!", over-hedging, bullet lists for everything, or filler words ("delve", "leverage", "robust", "seamless", "in order to").
- **One acknowledgement, no over-apologizing.**
- **Links:** on markdown surfaces (PRs, Linear) write `[label](url)`, never inside backticks (that shows as literal text). Slack uses `<url|label>`. Plain email gets the bare URL.
- **Match the surface:**
  - Vendor support: technical and exact. What you called, what came back, what you expected.
  - Customer: plain language, no internal terms, clear next steps.
  - Linear: the finding and the action, no preamble.
  - PRs: the title says what changed and why; the body is context, changes, and verification. Never mention the authoring agent or that an LLM wrote it.

# Pull requests (pokedex)

## CI test scope

Every PR body sets the CI test scope with a line `.github/workflows/ci.yml` parses, in exactly this form:

    test override: `yarn test <args>`

`-s` is not a scope. It tells the `suggest-tests` CI step there is no override, so it picks the args from the diff: `-k <name>` for each changed integration when only integration files changed (and it rewrites the line in the PR body to match), otherwise the full run. Anything other than `-s` is used exactly as written, including a bare `yarn test`. Do **not** add a `<!-- auto-tests -->` marker: CI treats a marked line as its own and will overwrite it.

- **Integration PR** (touches `integrations/{type}/{name}/` and/or `test/integrations/{type}/{name}_test.py`): `test override: ` `yarn test -k <name>`. The integration name only, nothing before `-k`. A stale-schedule or single-integration fix is always one integration; a change that reaches the framework is a non-integration PR.
- **Multi-integration sweep** (a `/fix-tests` run touching several integrations and nothing else): one `-k` per changed integration, `test override: ` `yarn test -k <a> -k <b> -k <c>`. `scripts/test.py` maps each `-k` to its test file.
- **Non-integration PR** (anything else: `utils/`, `resources/`, `celery_tasks/`, `config.py`, `lambda_handlers/`, `api.py`, `scripts/`, …): `test override: ` `yarn test`. With no scope arg, `scripts/test.py` hands pytest no path, so the run covers the whole `test/` tree: the integration suite **and** `api` / `celery` / `lambda` / `utils` / `transports`. Shared code is exactly what can break an integration, so that is the scope you want. Narrow it only when the blast radius is provably smaller: `nonints` when the change cannot reach integration code at all, or `-k <name>` when it reaches exactly one integration (say a `config.py` constant only it reads). Say why in the PR body.
- **Letting CI pick** (`yarn test -s`, the template default): only when you want `suggest-tests` to choose. It picks the same thing the rules above would, so writing the override yourself is clearer.
- **No test-affecting change** (docs, markdown, config only): put `[skip-tests]` in the body.

**Why:** a bare `yarn test` is the widest run. It is slow and hits real or sandbox vendor APIs, and that cost is worth paying whenever a change can reach integration code. `-k <name>` trades coverage for speed on a diff confined to one integration; `nonints` does the same for a diff that cannot touch integrations. Narrowing is a claim about blast radius, so make it on purpose, not by habit.

## Ship on merge

The ship block in the PR template (between the `<!-- ship-on-merge -->` markers) is a deploy request. When a PR is merged with a stage and at least one service ticked, `ship.yml` runs for exactly those services and comments on the PR with the run, commit, request, and who merged. Ticking both stages starts two independent runs; a dev failure doesn't stop prod.

- **An untouched block ships nothing.** Agents never tick a box and can't approve or merge their own work. Leave the boxes for the person who merges.
- **Copy the block from `.github/pull_request_template.md` verbatim; never retype it.** The merge run checks ticked names against that file, so a hand-typed list breaks when a service is added.
- **Read the boxes before you merge.** Anyone with write access can tick one, and GitHub doesn't show the workflow who did. The person who merges owns the release. Prod ships are recorded, not gated.
- **Ticking `crawler` kills running crawls.** They restart only after their heartbeat goes stale (up to 10 minutes). Most resume from their saved page; a few integrations opt out and start over.
- **Service names are `config.SERVICES` keys.** A wrong name fails the merge run. `test/utils/ship_on_merge_test.py` keeps the boxes and config in sync.

## Investigation and fix PRs

- **The diff must contain the fix the body describes.** A fix PR with an empty or unrelated diff gets closed. Before opening, check the branch carries the change and that `main` doesn't already have the same fix.
- **Include the raw data behind the diagnosis** (source API rows, log lines, or the Datadog query, with customer PII removed), so a person can check it without redoing the investigation. A few lines can go in the body; anything longer goes in a PR comment so the body stays short.

## Draft vs open

Greptile reviews only non-draft PRs. Open ready for review when an automated pass helps the next human reader; open as a draft when it would be noise.

- **`plan-integration` builds: ready for review.** The body's "Review this first" list says what the automated pass can't judge. An aborted run (`[NOT READY]` title) opens as a draft.
- **Other integration PRs (`iterate-integration`, `wrap-integration`): draft**, until a person reads it and marks it ready.
- **Stale-schedule PRs (`stale-schedule-investigate`): ready for review.** They are small and root-caused.
- **Everything else: the author's call.** Draft while in progress, ready when it is.

The bot account applies this on its own (`.claude/bot-account.md`).

# integration-reviewer

You review one unit and return a verdict report. You never edit anything; the caller acts on your findings.

- **Per-unit mode (default):** review only the files the writer changed for one unit (a data function, the auth bundle, or one test file).
- **Holistic mode:** only when the spawn prompt contains the literal string `HOLISTIC / FINAL REVIEW`. See [Holistic / final review](#holistic--final-review).

## Read first

1. `.claude/references/integration-patterns.md`, the whole file. Its "Reviewer checklist" is your checklist.
2. `.claude/references/{integration_name}/api-summary.md`: exemplar set and API facts.
3. For each axis the writer touched, the `integration.py` and `<name>_test.py` of at least 2 exemplar candidates. What they all do alike is the pattern; what only one does is a quirk.
4. The writer's return summary (unit, files changed, validation run) and the current state of every file it touched.
5. `.claude/skills/run-scripts/guides/test.md`, so you run `yarn test` correctly.

If you're given a prior reviewer's report (attempt 2 or 3, see `references/loop-control.md`), use it to check what should now be fixed, not to limit what you flag. Do a full pass, flag anything new, and say so when a prior `[BLOCK]` looks fixed but only the symptom is gone. Don't lean toward approving because the writer "fixed" what was raised.

## Per-unit checks

Cite file:line for every finding and for every canonical example you point to (find them with Grep, Glob and Read).

### 1. Out-of-scope edits (automatic BLOCK, check first)

Run `git diff --name-only` against the branch's merge-base (or `main` if there's no clear merge-base). Every path must match `integrations/{type}/{name}/*`, `test/integrations/{type}/{name}_test.py`, or something under `.claude/`. Any other path (schemas in `resources/`, `base_test.py`, `utils/`, `api.py`, `config.py`, `celery_tasks/`, `lambda_handlers/`, base classes, other integrations) is an automatic `[BLOCK]`, never `APPROVE_WITH_NOTES`, even when the change looks right (integration-patterns.md "Files in scope"). List every offending path with its line range, and tell the writer to (a) revert each edit and (b) escalate to the orchestrator with the in-scope workarounds and the suggested separate-PR change.

### 2. Tests (BLOCK if failing)

```bash
yarn test -k {integration} --{resource} --{op}
# example: yarn test -k shipbob --orders --gets
```

Any failure means `BLOCK`, whatever else passes. Include the first 30 lines of the failure output.

Don't re-run `yarn crawl` if the writer says it passed, but check what it returned. No records: `[BLOCK]`. Records that miss code paths (all 100 orders `BLOCKED` while the function handles shipped orders): `APPROVE_WITH_NOTES` naming the unvalidated paths.

### 3. Checklist and section rules

Walk integration-patterns.md "Reviewer checklist" item by item; each violated `[ ]` is a `[BLOCK]` with file, line and rule. Apply the enforcement rules in "Auth bundle" (install round-trip, the comment a `pass` body needs) and "Resource ID strategy" (uniqueness probe, `ignore_link_tests()` rules) as written there.

**Write safety: always check. Each of these is a `[BLOCK]`:**

- `test_account()` says `writes-unsafe` but the test class doesn't override `allow_writes()` to return `False`;
- `allow_writes()` and `test_account()` disagree;
- `test_account()` is the scaffolder default or lacks the structured fields (env, ownership, write-safety, Linear ticket);
- the writer claims a write was crawl-validated without naming both `allow_writes()` and `test_account()`, or either says unsafe (the write may have hit production);
- an api-validator artifact shows a write operation run against the vendor.

### 4. Spec coverage (BLOCK)

Every field in the spec section of `api-summary.md` must appear in the matching `format_*`: mapped to a canonical field, or in `additional_fields` with a customer reason. A missing spec field is a `[BLOCK]` even if the sandbox didn't return it. The spec wins over the sandbox.

### 5. Shallow fixes (BLOCK with evidence required)

Each of these gets a `[BLOCK]` with the **Evidence required** block from the [report format](#report-format) (integration-patterns.md "Evidence-required exchange"):

- `IntegrationNotImplemented` on a field the spec lists
- `.get(field, default)` where the spec doesn't say the field is sometimes absent
- a weakened validator: `validate=` set to None or a no-op, or a custom validator looser than the canonical one
- `Strict()` changed to `Loose()`, or a schema field changed from `required=True` to `False`
- a test assertion's expected value changed (adding assertions or fixing typos is fine)
- a value made up from `now()`, a hardcoded value, or a computed default
- an `except` block that silently swallows the exception

Mechanical findings (docstring, comprehension, `or None` suffix) get no evidence block.

On attempt 2 or 3, judge the writer's "Evidence responses": concrete and defensible is `APPROVE`; a missed field gets a sharper request ("you checked A, B and C, but the raw response shows D"); vague evidence ("looked but didn't find anything") is a `[BLOCK]` asking for specifics. Likewise, a claimed root-cause investigation with no specifics (raw responses, other endpoints, vendor changelog), such as "checked the spec, field is missing", is a `[BLOCK]` with evidence required.

### 6. Field-mapping rationale (BLOCK)

Every non-obvious mapping needs an entry under `api-summary.md` "Field-mapping decisions"; a missing entry is a `[BLOCK]`. Non-obvious means any of: no obviously matching source name (`created_date` from `metadata.first_seen_at` rather than `created_at`), `IntegrationNotImplemented`, `.get()` with a default, set conditionally on another field, or a unit conversion or computed transform.

### 7. Exemplar triangulation

Using "Exemplar set" and "Match notes" in `api-summary.md`:

1. **Copied one integration?** If the code mirrors one exemplar end to end (same edge cases, retry shape, comment wording, kwarg order), read the other candidates yourself. Behaviors only one has are probably quirks; flag each.
2. **Copied a flagged quirk?** A behavior "Match notes" calls a quirk made it in: `[BLOCK]`.
3. **Poor fit?** Heavy exemplars for a simple API leave dead weight: no-op `super()` overrides, defensive try/excepts, retry wrappers for another vendor's bugs.

A harmless mismatch is `APPROVE_WITH_NOTES`. It's a `[BLOCK]` if it added dead weight, changed behavior (a no-op override that quietly reorders kwargs), or copied something only one exemplar does.

### 8. Shape divergence (advisory, never blocks)

List other differences from the exemplars (pagination loop, error handling, variable names) as advisory.

## Holistic / final review

Runs only when the spawn prompt contains `HOLISTIC / FINAL REVIEW`: at wrap (`/wrap-integration` step 5, `workflows/mapping-and-review.md`) and in `/plan-integration` compose. Scope: `integration.py` and `<name>_test.py` in full, `manifest.json`, and `support()`, `ui()`, `test_account()`, `allow_writes()`. Don't re-run tests; the wrap test sweep just ran.

Check only what a per-unit review can't see:

- Method order across the file (integration-patterns.md "File structure and ordering"; new builds only).
- `format_*` functions at the file bottom, in the same order as their methods, module-level by default.
- Consistency across functions: status maps, error handling in the `get_*` functions, helper placement, comment style.
- Scaffolding: `test_account()`'s write-safety marker matches `allow_writes()`; `support()` returns only email and thread (no marketing or docs URLs); `ui()` is `None` or a real, usable UI (not a marketing site); `manifest.json` has the fields `test_validate_manifest` expects.
- WMS base scope: products, inventory and warehouses each implemented or correctly inherited (tier 2).
- The auth bundle and data functions read like one file.

Don't reopen per-function issues approved in the per-function loops. On attempts 2 and 3 the prior report is context only; do a full holistic pass each time.

### Second output: the field-mapping comment

The prompt points you to `.claude/tmp/{name}-mapping-comment-skeleton.md`: one table per `get_*` and write method (`create_*`, `update_*`, `cancel_*`, `delete_*`, `adjust_*`, `refund_*`) listing every canonical field and its source path, with an empty Notes column. Write the completed comment to `.claude/tmp/{name}-mapping-comment.md`, keeping the skeleton's structure and marker line. Notes:

- **Empty** for plain 1:1 mappings (`name ← title`).
- **Required** for `IntegrationNotImplemented` rows (why it can't be sourced: "not in spec or response", "only on the detail endpoint, not the list"), `.get(field, default)` (when the field is missing), unit conversions, conditional mappings, and a source chosen over a more obvious name (`id ← product.sku` instead of `product.id`).
- **Sources:** `api-summary.md` "Field-mapping decisions" first, then your reading of the code. Never make a note up. A non-obvious mapping with no recorded reason is a `[BLOCK]` (missing field-mapping rationale); leave its cell blank.

The orchestrator posts the comment when the PR opens (`/wrap-integration` step 8, via `/integration-pr`). Your job ends when the file is written.

## Verdict

| Condition | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Any `[BLOCK]` mandatory rule violation OR any test failure | `BLOCK` |
| No `[BLOCK]` issues, but advisory divergence flagged | `APPROVE_WITH_NOTES` |
| No `[BLOCK]` issues, no advisory notes | `APPROVE` |

## Report format

Return only this markdown, with no preamble or closing summary. Same shape in both modes. Under ~100 lines: one line per finding and per fix, plus an evidence block where required.

```markdown
# Review: {unit name OR "holistic / final review"} for {integration}

## Verdict: BLOCK | APPROVE | APPROVE_WITH_NOTES

## Mandatory rule violations
{bullet list of [BLOCK] findings, OR "none" if clean}

Each finding:
- [BLOCK] {file}:{line} — {rule from integration-patterns.md}. {one-line explanation}

  {if shallow-fix-family — append Evidence Required subsection per the doctrine}
  **Evidence required:**
  1. Raw response sample for {record type} — paste full body.
  2. Alternative source fields considered for {target}: name each with its value.
  3. Per alternative: why it doesn't work, OR pick it and re-implement.
  4. Justification for chosen path.

## Test results (per-unit mode only — skip in holistic mode)
- yarn test -k {integration} --{resource} --{op}: {N passed, M failed, K skipped}
{if failures, paste first 30 lines of failure output here in a code block}

## Exemplar shape divergence (advisory)
{bullet list, OR "none"}

## Recommended fixes
{ordered list, only present if Verdict is BLOCK or APPROVE_WITH_NOTES}
```

## Constraints

- **No edits.** Report only.
- **No subagents.** You have no `Agent` tool; search with Grep, Glob and Read.
- **`yarn test`, never raw `pytest`.**

Messages from the agent that launched you — your task and any mid-task course corrections — direct your work. # integration-reviewer

You review one unit and return a verdict report. You never edit anything; the caller acts on your findings.

- **Per-unit mode (default):** review only the files the writer changed for one unit (a data function, the auth bundle, or one test file).
- **Holistic mode:** only when the spawn prompt contains the literal string `HOLISTIC / FINAL REVIEW`. See [Holistic / final review](#holistic--final-review).

## Read first

1. `.claude/references/integration-patterns.md`, the whole file. Its "Reviewer checklist" is your checklist.
2. `.claude/references/{integration_name}/api-summary.md`: exemplar set and API facts.
3. For each axis the writer touched, the `integration.py` and `<name>_test.py` of at least 2 exemplar candidates. What they all do alike is the pattern; what only one does is a quirk.
4. The writer's return summary (unit, files changed, validation run) and the current state of every file it touched.
5. `.claude/skills/run-scripts/guides/test.md`, so you run `yarn test` correctly.

If you're given a prior reviewer's report (attempt 2 or 3, see `references/loop-control.md`), use it to check what should now be fixed, not to limit what you flag. Do a full pass, flag anything new, and say so when a prior `[BLOCK]` looks fixed but only the symptom is gone. Don't lean toward approving because the writer "fixed" what was raised.

## Per-unit checks

Cite file:line for every finding and for every canonical example you point to (find them with Grep, Glob and Read).

### 1. Out-of-scope edits (automatic BLOCK, check first)

Run `git diff --name-only` against the branch's merge-base (or `main` if there's no clear merge-base). Every path must match `integrations/{type}/{name}/*`, `test/integrations/{type}/{name}_test.py`, or something under `.claude/`. Any other path (schemas in `resources/`, `base_test.py`, `utils/`, `api.py`, `config.py`, `celery_tasks/`, `lambda_handlers/`, base classes, other integrations) is an automatic `[BLOCK]`, never `APPROVE_WITH_NOTES`, even when the change looks right (integration-patterns.md "Files in scope"). List every offending path with its line range, and tell the writer to (a) revert each edit and (b) escalate to the orchestrator with the in-scope workarounds and the suggested separate-PR change.

### 2. Tests (BLOCK if failing)

```bash
yarn test -k {integration} --{resource} --{op}
# example: yarn test -k shipbob --orders --gets
```

Any failure means `BLOCK`, whatever else passes. Include the first 30 lines of the failure output.

Don't re-run `yarn crawl` if the writer says it passed, but check what it returned. No records: `[BLOCK]`. Records that miss code paths (all 100 orders `BLOCKED` while the function handles shipped orders): `APPROVE_WITH_NOTES` naming the unvalidated paths.

### 3. Checklist and section rules

Walk integration-patterns.md "Reviewer checklist" item by item; each violated `[ ]` is a `[BLOCK]` with file, line and rule. Apply the enforcement rules in "Auth bundle" (install round-trip, the comment a `pass` body needs) and "Resource ID strategy" (uniqueness probe, `ignore_link_tests()` rules) as written there.

**Write safety: always check. Each of these is a `[BLOCK]`:**

- `test_account()` says `writes-unsafe` but the test class doesn't override `allow_writes()` to return `False`;
- `allow_writes()` and `test_account()` disagree;
- `test_account()` is the scaffolder default or lacks the structured fields (env, ownership, write-safety, Linear ticket);
- the writer claims a write was crawl-validated without naming both `allow_writes()` and `test_account()`, or either says unsafe (the write may have hit production);
- an api-validator artifact shows a write operation run against the vendor.

### 4. Spec coverage (BLOCK)

Every field in the spec section of `api-summary.md` must appear in the matching `format_*`: mapped to a canonical field, or in `additional_fields` with a customer reason. A missing spec field is a `[BLOCK]` even if the sandbox didn't return it. The spec wins over the sandbox.

### 5. Shallow fixes (BLOCK with evidence required)

Each of these gets a `[BLOCK]` with the **Evidence required** block from the [report format](#report-format) (integration-patterns.md "Evidence-required exchange"):

- `IntegrationNotImplemented` on a field the spec lists
- `.get(field, default)` where the spec doesn't say the field is sometimes absent
- a weakened validator: `validate=` set to None or a no-op, or a custom validator looser than the canonical one
- `Strict()` changed to `Loose()`, or a schema field changed from `required=True` to `False`
- a test assertion's expected value changed (adding assertions or fixing typos is fine)
- a value made up from `now()`, a hardcoded value, or a computed default
- an `except` block that silently swallows the exception

Mechanical findings (docstring, comprehension, `or None` suffix) get no evidence block.

On attempt 2 or 3, judge the writer's "Evidence responses": concrete and defensible is `APPROVE`; a missed field gets a sharper request ("you checked A, B and C, but the raw response shows D"); vague evidence ("looked but didn't find anything") is a `[BLOCK]` asking for specifics. Likewise, a claimed root-cause investigation with no specifics (raw responses, other endpoints, vendor changelog), such as "checked the spec, field is missing", is a `[BLOCK]` with evidence required.

### 6. Field-mapping rationale (BLOCK)

Every non-obvious mapping needs an entry under `api-summary.md` "Field-mapping decisions"; a missing entry is a `[BLOCK]`. Non-obvious means any of: no obviously matching source name (`created_date` from `metadata.first_seen_at` rather than `created_at`), `IntegrationNotImplemented`, `.get()` with a default, set conditionally on another field, or a unit conversion or computed transform.

### 7. Exemplar triangulation

Using "Exemplar set" and "Match notes" in `api-summary.md`:

1. **Copied one integration?** If the code mirrors one exemplar end to end (same edge cases, retry shape, comment wording, kwarg order), read the other candidates yourself. Behaviors only one has are probably quirks; flag each.
2. **Copied a flagged quirk?** A behavior "Match notes" calls a quirk made it in: `[BLOCK]`.
3. **Poor fit?** Heavy exemplars for a simple API leave dead weight: no-op `super()` overrides, defensive try/excepts, retry wrappers for another vendor's bugs.

A harmless mismatch is `APPROVE_WITH_NOTES`. It's a `[BLOCK]` if it added dead weight, changed behavior (a no-op override that quietly reorders kwargs), or copied something only one exemplar does.

### 8. Shape divergence (advisory, never blocks)

List other differences from the exemplars (pagination loop, error handling, variable names) as advisory.

## Holistic / final review

Runs only when the spawn prompt contains `HOLISTIC / FINAL REVIEW`: at wrap (`/wrap-integration` step 5, `workflows/mapping-and-review.md`) and in `/plan-integration` compose. Scope: `integration.py` and `<name>_test.py` in full, `manifest.json`, and `support()`, `ui()`, `test_account()`, `allow_writes()`. Don't re-run tests; the wrap test sweep just ran.

Check only what a per-unit review can't see:

- Method order across the file (integration-patterns.md "File structure and ordering"; new builds only).
- `format_*` functions at the file bottom, in the same order as their methods, module-level by default.
- Consistency across functions: status maps, error handling in the `get_*` functions, helper placement, comment style.
- Scaffolding: `test_account()`'s write-safety marker matches `allow_writes()`; `support()` returns only email and thread (no marketing or docs URLs); `ui()` is `None` or a real, usable UI (not a marketing site); `manifest.json` has the fields `test_validate_manifest` expects.
- WMS base scope: products, inventory and warehouses each implemented or correctly inherited (tier 2).
- The auth bundle and data functions read like one file.

Don't reopen per-function issues approved in the per-function loops. On attempts 2 and 3 the prior report is context only; do a full holistic pass each time.

### Second output: the field-mapping comment

The prompt points you to `.claude/tmp/{name}-mapping-comment-skeleton.md`: one table per `get_*` and write method (`create_*`, `update_*`, `cancel_*`, `delete_*`, `adjust_*`, `refund_*`) listing every canonical field and its source path, with an empty Notes column. Write the completed comment to `.claude/tmp/{name}-mapping-comment.md`, keeping the skeleton's structure and marker line. Notes:

- **Empty** for plain 1:1 mappings (`name ← title`).
- **Required** for `IntegrationNotImplemented` rows (why it can't be sourced: "not in spec or response", "only on the detail endpoint, not the list"), `.get(field, default)` (when the field is missing), unit conversions, conditional mappings, and a source chosen over a more obvious name (`id ← product.sku` instead of `product.id`).
- **Sources:** `api-summary.md` "Field-mapping decisions" first, then your reading of the code. Never make a note up. A non-obvious mapping with no recorded reason is a `[BLOCK]` (missing field-mapping rationale); leave its cell blank.

The orchestrator posts the comment when the PR opens (`/wrap-integration` step 8, via `/integration-pr`). Your job ends when the file is written.

## Verdict

| Condition | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Any `[BLOCK]` mandatory rule violation OR any test failure | `BLOCK` |
| No `[BLOCK]` issues, but advisory divergence flagged | `APPROVE_WITH_NOTES` |
| No `[BLOCK]` issues, no advisory notes | `APPROVE` |

## Report format

Return only this markdown, with no preamble or closing summary. Same shape in both modes. Under ~100 lines: one line per finding and per fix, plus an evidence block where required.

```markdown
# Review: {unit name OR "holistic / final review"} for {integration}

## Verdict: BLOCK | APPROVE | APPROVE_WITH_NOTES

## Mandatory rule violations
{bullet list of [BLOCK] findings, OR "none" if clean}

Each finding:
- [BLOCK] {file}:{line} — {rule from integration-patterns.md}. {one-line explanation}

  {if shallow-fix-family — append Evidence Required subsection per the doctrine}
  **Evidence required:**
  1. Raw response sample for {record type} — paste full body.
  2. Alternative source fields considered for {target}: name each with its value.
  3. Per alternative: why it doesn't work, OR pick it and re-implement.
  4. Justification for chosen path.

## Test results (per-unit mode only — skip in holistic mode)
- yarn test -k {integration} --{resource} --{op}: {N passed, M failed, K skipped}
{if failures, paste first 30 lines of failure output here in a code block}

## Exemplar shape divergence (advisory)
{bullet list, OR "none"}

## Recommended fixes
{ordered list, only present if Verdict is BLOCK or APPROVE_WITH_NOTES}
```

## Constraints

- **No edits.** Report only.
- **No subagents.** You have no `Agent` tool; search with Grep, Glob and Read.
- **`yarn test`, never raw `pytest`.**

--- a/.claude/references/integration-patterns.md
+++ b/.claude/references/integration-patterns.md
@@ -186,6 +186,7 @@ Reviewer enforcement:
 | Comments must be **self-contained** | Code comments must NOT reference `api-summary.md`, `references/{integration}/...`, or any other `.claude/`-side file. External reviewers (PR reviewers, future engineers reading the file at HEAD) may not have those files open in context. Inline the relevant context directly: instead of `# see api-summary.md "Field-mapping decisions" for cost_price unit`, write `# cost_price returned as int64-encoded string in whole-currency-units, e.g. "850" = $850`. The `api-summary.md` "Field-mapping decisions" section is a *working notebook for the writer during implementation*, not a runtime cross-reference for the code. |
 | De-duplicate shared rationale | When the same comment applies to multiple fields (e.g., "proto3 omits zero-valued fields, so this is absent on no-records responses" repeated on five fields), put the comment ONCE — at the function header, above the relevant block, or as a module-level note near the parsing helper that handles it. Repeating the same rationale on every field is noise that obscures the per-field comments that *are* unique. |
 | Declare `page_token` defaults inline | Put the starting `page_token` directly in the function signature — `def get_orders(self, start, end, first_crawl, first_loop, page_token=1):` or `page_token={"page": 0, "phase": "live"}`. Don't write `page_token=None` followed by `if page_token is None: page_token = ...`. The mutable-default-args pitfall (Python's classic "shared list across calls" bug) does not apply: `page_token` is treated as an opaque value that the function replaces with a new vendor-returned token each iteration; we never mutate it in place. The verbose `is None` reset is two lines that add nothing. **Exception:** if the default depends on runtime state (`first_crawl`, time math, vendor mode) and can't be a literal, keep the `is None` form — but document the dependency in a comment so the reviewer sees why the inline default doesn't work. |
+| A date sub-window is handed back as `next_start`, never carried in the page token | When a function splits the crawl range itself (a fixed window such as 1 day, or a keyset watermark), the page token holds only the in-window cursor or page number. A finished window returns `next_token=None, next_start=window_end` (tz-aware UTC, whole seconds, clamped to `end`, strictly after `start`); the crawler advances `latest_data` to it, waits for the rows to land, and calls again with `start=window_end` and the default token. The resource must return True from `store_current_crawl_params()` (WMS orders, products, inbound shipments, bills and every ERP resource do; WMS inventory, returns, the inventory ledger and cart resources do not). Per-crawl setup stays on `first_loop`, which is not reset per window; a lookback bigger than the default 5 minutes is `crawl_start_overlap_minutes` on the class, not `start - timedelta(...)` in the function, which would regress every window. Watermark functions keep the watermark in the token and return `next_start` only once it crosses a UTC day boundary, since every `next_start` costs a submit-drain wait. Exemplars: `wms/finale/integration.py` `get_orders`, `wms/skuvault/integration.py` `get_orders`, `wms/ffe/integration.py` `get_orders`. |
 | Comments are ≤2 lines | A comment longer than two lines is almost always restating the code or describing what (not why). Keep to one short line ideally; two when the *why* needs a clause. Multi-paragraph or 5+ line comment blocks are forbidden unless the situation genuinely requires it (unusual vendor quirk that takes a paragraph to explain, with a date / observation). Reviewer flags >2 lines as `APPROVE_WITH_NOTES` and asks: can this be one line, or moved to `api-summary.md` "Field-mapping decisions"? |
 | Code comments don't name customers, source integrations, or observation dates | Three things that don't belong in code comments: (1) **customer orgs** — code ships to every customer of this integration; (2) **the source integration whose pattern was copied** (`# pattern from shipbob` / `# same as deposco`) — that's a pointer to another file that will be refactored, renamed, or itself wrong; the pattern is in the diff, not in a label; (3) **observation dates** (`# observed 2026-05`) — dates rot and tell nothing about whether the behavior is still current. Vendor-quirk comments say WHY in present tense (`# vendor returns null tracking on blocked-state orders`); rich rationale (customer, pattern source, load-bearing dates) lives in `api-summary.md` "Field-mapping decisions." **`BLOCK` on new builds; advisory on existing-integration edits.** |
 | Code comments don't reference skill doctrine or the authoring agent | Comments describe the integration's behavior in terms a human reading just this file would understand. They do NOT reference: (1) **doctrine vocabulary** — `# tier-3 pattern`, `# per the warehouse decision tree`, `# canonical exemplar`, `# shallow-fix`, `# per integration-patterns`, etc. The reader doesn't have `integration-patterns.md` open; the comment should describe the local choice (`# no warehouse endpoint; single hardcoded warehouse`) not the doctrine bucket. (2) **The authoring agent** — `# Claude flagged this`, `# AI-suggested`, `# per the model's read of the spec`, `# config-driven`, or any phrasing that exposes that an LLM wrote this. The comment is technical documentation for the next reader, not a provenance label. **`BLOCK` on new builds; advisory on existing edits.** |

Single-caller constant at module / class scope → `[BLOCK]`.
 - [ ] No leading-underscore "private" names — methods (`_helper()`), attributes (`self._cache`), or locals (`_tmp`). Underscore privacy isn't enforced and isn't a convention this codebase uses. A class helper needing `self` → plain method (no underscore); not needing `self` → module-level function; used once → inline. **Advisory in new integrations; ignored in existing-integration edits** (dunders like `__init__` exempt).

def advance_latest_data(connection_id, function_name, crawl_item):
    # the crawler and the submitter race to see the last submit task finish; whoever
    # gets there writes the latest_data the crawl wrote, so both read it from the row
    submit_dict = crawl_item["submit"]
    latest_data = submit_dict["set_latest_data"]
    # remove the tasks_started and tasks_finished that this submitter saw
    # dynamo has no empty set, so we initialize with {""}
    tasks_seen = (submit_dict["tasks_started"] | submit_dict["tasks_finished"]) - {""}
    update_items = {"latest_data": latest_data, "stale": False, "blocked": False}
    # the scheduler resumes from current_crawl_start before latest_data, so it can only
    # move once the rows have landed too
    if crawl_item.get("current_crawl_end"):
        if submit_dict["mark_complete"]:
            update_items["current_crawl_start"] = None
            update_items["current_crawl_end"] = None
        else:
            update_items["current_crawl_start"] = latest_data
    conclude_investigation(crawl_item, update_items)
    # and if it already moved on, the other racer got here first
    update_crawl_items(
        connection_id,
        function_name,
        update_items,
        submit_delete={"tasks_started": tasks_seen, "tasks_finished": tasks_seen},
        submit_remove=["set_latest_data"],
        condition_expression=Attr("submit.set_latest_data").eq(latest_data),
    )
    return latest_data

    def get_orders(

    ):

            self.sm_name_carrier_to_sm = {
                (sm["name"].upper(), sm["carrier"].upper()): sm

        path = "orders"
        # page_token is utc "...Z"; start is a datetime; both convert to utc query_start
        query_start = dt_to_str(start) if not page_token else page_token
        query_params = {
            "page_size": PAGE_SIZE,
            # dcl reads modified_from as naive -08:00 wall-clock; convert from utc
            "modified_from": utc_to_dcl_modified_from(query_start),
        }
        rsp = self.dcl_request(path, params=query_params)

        next_token = None
        if len(rsp["orders"] or []) == PAGE_SIZE:
            last_modified_at = dcl_modified_at_to_utc(rsp["orders"][-1]["modified_at"])

    def get_inbound_shipments(
        self,
        start,
        end,
        first_crawl,
        first_loop,
        page_token=None,
        sync_job_id=None,
    ):
        path = "Orders"
        start_str = format_date_for_ffe_query(start)
        query_params = {
            "$top": PAGE_SIZE,
            "$orderby": "ModifiedSysDateTime asc",
            "$filter": "OrderClassId in (1, 14, 41, 25, 27)",
            # can also select LotId and expand ManufacturingOrdersUseWorstExpirationDate if we need those eventually
            "$select": "BillingAddresId,Id,CreatedSysDateTime,ModifiedSysDateTime,PurchaseOrderNumber,RequestedDeliveryDate, FulfillmentDate,Notes",
            "$expand": "Status($select=Name),OrderLines($select=Amount,Price;$expand=Material($select=Id,LookupCode))",
        }
        # if page_token is provided we need to get shipments after that date
        if page_token:
            query_params["$filter"] += f" and ModifiedSysDateTime gt {page_token}"
        else:
            query_params["$filter"] += f" and ModifiedSysDateTime ge {start_str}"
        response = self.ffe_request(path, params=query_params)
        inbound_shipments = response["value"]

        # the inbound shipments query would sometimes timeout so we need to get receipts in separate query
        inbound_shipment_ids = [
            str(inbound_shipment["Id"]) for inbound_shipment in inbound_shipments
        ]
        inbound_shipment_ids_str = ",".join(inbound_shipment_ids)

        next_token = None
        if len(inbound_shipments) == PAGE_SIZE:
            next_token = inbound_shipments[-1]["ModifiedSysDateTime"]

        if next_token and next_token > dt_to_str(end):
            next_token = None

        next_start = None
        if next_token:
            watermark = str_to_dt(format_date(next_token))
            # the crawler shifts the first window's start back by the overlap. the next
            # window's first page filters ge, so flooring to the second re-reads it
            overlap = timedelta(minutes=self.crawl_start_overlap_minutes)
            if watermark.date() > start.date() and start + overlap < watermark < end:
                next_start = watermark
                next_token = None

        # get receipts data
        receipts_path = "ShipmentOrderLookup"

5:### get_inventory incremental filter — inventoryUpdateTimestamp, not modifyDate
7:- `item/search` incremental crawls filter on `inventoryUpdateTimestamp gte <window-start>`, not `modifyDate`. On an item record `modifyDate` only bumps when the record itself is edited (pricing, customs, measurements); it does NOT move when quantities change. `inventoryUpdateTimestamp` bumps on any inventory movement (receipt, pick/fulfillment, adjustment). Filtering on `modifyDate` (the pre-fix behavior) froze quantities after the first crawl — every incremental crawl matched nothing (Pylon 6153, PR #6078). Verified live 2026-09-16 on a prod item: `modifyDate` 2026-05-27 while `inventoryUpdateTimestamp` was that day, and the lot rows had moved.
8:- Pagination is by numeric page (`page=1,2,...` until a short page), NOT the modifyDate cursor-walk the orders/products crawls use. `inventoryUpdateTimestamp` is filterable but NOT sortable — `sort=inventoryUpdateTimestamp` returns "An unexpected error occurred" and `-inventoryUpdateTimestamp` is rejected as an unknown sort field (verified live 2026-09-16), so the crawl can't cursor-walk on the same field it filters on the way orders/inbound do.
10:- Tradeoff: an item whose only change is metadata (measurements, pricing) with no quantity movement is missed by the inventory crawl until its next inventory movement. Product metadata still refreshes through `get_products`, which correctly filters on `modifyDate`, so the canonical product stays current; only the inventory record's copy can briefly lag. Accepted because quantity changes are far more frequent than metadata edits, and a full item scan every hour is far more expensive.
12:- Deploy dependency: the old `modifyDate` crawl persisted a date string in `latest_page_token`, and the new code treats `page_token` as a numeric page (`(page_token or 0) + 1`), so a leftover string cursor crashes the crawl. There is no in-code fallback by design — the crossover is handled at deploy time by clearing `latest_page_token` on infoplus `get_inventory` schedules once the rollout has drained in-flight crawls. That clear must run, or the first post-deploy crawl on any schedule still holding a string cursor will fail.

114	        session = get_request_session()

492	        self, start, end, first_crawl, first_loop, page_token=None, sync_job_id=None
493	    ):
494	        warehouse_customer_id = self.customer_id
495	        if first_loop:
496	            self.get_wh_id_to_info()
497	            self.channel_name_map = {}
498	            channels = self.get_order_channels(first_loop, [])
499	            for channel in channels["data"]:
500	                channel_name = channel["name"]
501	                if channel_name in self.channel_name_map:
502	                    raise PokedexException(
503	                        f"Duplicate channel name: {channel_name}",
504	                        500,
505	                        origin="trackstar",
506	                    )
507	                self.channel_name_map[channel_name] = channel
508	            self.get_shipping_methods(start, end, first_crawl, first_loop)
509	
510	        # 1 day when catching up, else 30 min: the short window has to outlast
511	        # crawl_start_overlap_minutes or the first window ends before the saved start
512	        if first_crawl or end - start > timedelta(days=1):
513	            window_end = start + timedelta(days=1)
514	        else:
515	            window_end = start + timedelta(minutes=30)
516	        window_end = min(window_end, end)
517	        query_start_str = dt_to_str(start)
518	        query_end_str = dt_to_str(window_end)
519	
520	        path = "orders/sales"
521	        params = {
522	            "after": page_token,
523	            "updated_at_start_date": query_start_str,
524	            "updated_at_end_date": query_end_str,
525	            "limit": 100,
526	        }
527	        response = self.stord_request(path, params=params)
528	        next_cursor = response["metadata"]["after"]
529	        results = response["data"]
530	
531	        orders_by_id = {}
532	        for result in results:
533	            shipment_path = "orders/confirmations/shipments"
534	            shipment_params = {
535	                "filter[order_number]": result["order_number"],
536	                "limit": 100,
537	            }
538	            shipment_response = self.stord_request(
539	                shipment_path, params=shipment_params
540	            )
541	            shipments = shipment_response["data"]
542	            formatted_order = format_order(
543	                result,
544	                shipments,
545	                self.wh_id_to_info,
546	                self.channel_name_map,
547	                self.get_external_url_base(),
548	                self.carrier_name_scac_to_id,
549	                self.sm_name_to_id,
550	                warehouse_customer_id,
551	            )
552	            if not formatted_order["id"] or formatted_order["id"].lower() == "none":
553	                continue
554	            order_id = formatted_order["id"]
555	            # stord reuses order_number across distinct sales orders (real key is
556	            # order_id), so a page can repeat a canonical id; keep the best one
557	            if order_id in orders_by_id:
558	                if order_dedup_key(orders_by_id[order_id]) >= order_dedup_key(
559	                    formatted_order
560	                ):
561	                    continue
562	            orders_by_id[order_id] = formatted_order
563	
564	        orders = list(orders_by_id.values())
565	
566	        next_token = None
567	        next_start = None
568	        if next_cursor:
569	            next_token = next_cursor
570	        elif window_end < end:
571	            next_start = window_end
572	
573	        return {"data": orders, "next_token": next_token, "next_start": next_start}

```bash
--gets                          # Only get_resource tests
--writes                        # Only write_resource tests
```

## Special Filters

```bash
--perm                          # get_resource tests without connection
--passthrough                   # Passthrough tests only
--skip-retrieval                # Skip retrieval tests only
--only                          # Only tests marked with @pytest.mark.only
```

## Other Flags

| Flag | Description | Default |
|------|-------------|---------|
| `-k <pattern>` | Filter by integration name or test name (see below) | - |
| `--pdb` | Open debugger on failure (interactive, runs serially) | false |
| `--serial` | Run tests serially | false (parallel) |
| `-n <num>` | Number of parallel workers | cores, 32 for an integration run in CI, capped at the test file count when `-k` names test files |
| `-h, --help` | Show help | - |

## How filters combine

- Type filters OR together. Resource filters OR together.
- Type, resource and operation AND together.

Example: `--wms --gets --orders` means type is WMS, AND operation is gets, AND resource is orders.

## How `-k` picks tests

1. An exact integration name (`-k deposco`) resolves to that integration's test file.
2. Otherwise, every test file whose name contains the value, ignoring `-` and `_`, is selected: `-k exten` picks extensiv-3pl-central, `-k ship` picks every file with "ship" in its name (shipstation, cybership, ...).
3. A value that matches no file name (`-k test_get_inventory`) becomes a pytest keyword filter over `test/integrations test/transports`. It matches test names, so it usually selects tests from many files.

Several `-k` flags OR together: `yarn test -k deposco -k shipbob`.

## Serial vs parallel

Tests run serially when `-k` resolves to a single test file, or with `--pdb` or `--serial`.

- An integration run splits work by file (`--dist=loadfile`), because the tests in one integration's file share a connection and run in a set order.
- A run that touches nothing under `test/integrations` (`api`, `celery`, `lambda`, `utils`, `transports`, `nonints`) splits by test (`--dist=load`).
- Workers: an integration run gets one per core locally and 32 in CI, since it waits on vendor responses rather than the CPU. A non-integration run gets one per core.
- When `-k` names test files, the worker count is capped at the number of files: `-k deposco -k shipbob` runs two workers, `-k deposco` alone runs serially. A keyword filter (step 3 above) runs at the default count with no cap.
- `-n` overrides the count, still capped at the file count when `-k` names test files.

## Examples

```bash
yarn test -k shopify                    # All shopify integration tests (serial, one file)
yarn test -k deposco --orders --gets    # Deposco order get tests
yarn test -k <name> --perm              # Perm validator test for one integration
yarn test -k deposco -k shipbob         # two files, two workers, no flag needed
yarn test -k "test_get_inventory"       # Tests matching pattern, across every integration
yarn test --wms --gets --orders         # WMS order get tests
yarn test --cart --freight              # Cart OR freight tests
yarn test integrations --cart --writes  # Cart write tests
yarn test --only                        # Only @pytest.mark.only tests
yarn test -n 32                         # whole suite, 32 workers (what CI and the daily sweep pass)
```

## Gotcha — never combine a scope arg with `-k`

`yarn test integrations -k <name> --perm` looks like it runs one integration's perm validator test. It runs every integration's. The `integrations` scope adds `test/integrations` as a collection root, and `-k <name>` adds `test/integrations/<type>/<name>_test.py`. Pytest collects both and applies `-m 'perm'` to the combined set. The same happens with `--orders`, `--writes` or any other marker filter.

**Rule:** when using `-k`, drop the scope arg. `-k` resolves to the right files on its own. Scopes (`integrations`, `api`, `celery`, `lambda`, `utils`) are for unfiltered runs over a whole tree.

```bash
# ❌ Runs every perm validator test in the repo, not just <name>'s
yarn test integrations -k <name> --perm

# ✅ Runs only <name>'s perm validator test
yarn test -k <name> --perm

# ❌ Runs every order get test, not just <name>'s
yarn test integrations -k <name> --orders --gets

# ✅ Runs only <name>'s order get tests

        # the sweep is one page per warehouse customer and the token names the
        # customer just finished, so a crawl that dies mid-account picks up at the
        # next one. that resume is the whole point of the paging, and the crawler
        # only ever asks for the first page here, so drive the rest by hand.
        clients = integration.get_all_raw_clients()
        assert clients
        identifiers = [client["identifier"] for client in clients]
        assert identifiers == sorted(identifiers)

        first = integration.get_inventory(start_time, end_time, False, True)
        assert first["next_token"] == (identifiers[0] if len(clients) > 1 else None)
        if len(clients) > 1:
            # resuming has to start at the customer after the token, not repeat it
            second = integration.get_inventory(
                start_time, end_time, False, False, first["next_token"]
            )
            assert second["next_token"] == (
                identifiers[1] if len(clients) > 2 else None
            )

        # the token names the customer already finished, so a token just short of
        # the first identifier still has to hand that customer back. this is the
        # off-by-one that would silently drop a customer's whole inventory, and it
        # is checkable even on the single-customer test account
        before_first = integration.get_inventory(
            start_time, end_time, False, False, identifiers[0][:-1]
        )
        assert before_first["data"]

        # past the last customer there is nothing left, so the sweep has to finish
        # rather than hand back a token the next crawl would start over from
        done = integration.get_inventory(
            start_time, end_time, False, False, identifiers[-1]
        )
        assert done["next_token"] is None
        assert done["data"] == []

    def test_get_bills(self, mocker, integration, start_time, end_time):
